title: Exodus IQ
subtitle: From the burning bush to the parted sea, how well do you know it?

questions.text: How was baby Moses saved from Pharaoh's order to kill the Hebrew boys?

options.text: He was hidden in a basket among the reeds of the river
options.explanation: Exodus 2 says his mother made an ark of bulrushes and placed him among the reeds by the river's bank.

options.text: He was raised in secret by shepherds
options.explanation: Moses did become a shepherd later in Midian, but as a baby he was hidden in a basket on the river.

options.text: An angel carried him to safety
options.explanation: There is no angel in this scene. His mother hid him in a basket and his sister watched over him.

options.text: He was smuggled out of Egypt by traders
options.explanation: Moses stayed in Egypt and was actually raised in Pharaoh's own household.

questions.text: Who found baby Moses and raised him?

options.explanation: Exodus 2 tells how Pharaoh's daughter found the basket at the river and raised the child as her own.
The midwives Shiphrah and Puah feared God and spared the boys, but it was Pharaoh's daughter who raised Moses.
Aaron was Moses' brother, not the one who found and raised him.
No priest is mentioned here. Pharaoh's daughter drew him from the water and raised him.

questions.text: How did God first speak to Moses in the wilderness?

options.explanation: God spoke to others through dreams elsewhere, but Moses met God at a burning bush.

options.text: From a bush that burned but was not consumed
options.explanation: Exodus 3 describes the bush burning with fire yet not consumed, and God calling to Moses from it.
There was no priesthood yet at this point. God spoke directly from the burning bush.

options.text: By writing on a stone tablet
options.explanation: Stone tablets came later at Sinai. The first encounter was at the burning bush.

questions.text: When Moses asked God's name, what did God say?

options.explanation: Exodus 3:14 (ASV) reads, "And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you."
That is not how God answered. The name given was tied to His eternal being, I AM.
God did reveal His name to Moses rather than hiding it.
Most High is a title used elsewhere, but the answer at the bush was I AM THAT I AM.

questions.text: Who did God send to help Moses speak to Pharaoh?

options.explanation: Miriam was a prophetess and led the women in song, but the spokesman God appointed was Aaron.
Exodus 4 says Aaron, Moses' brother, would speak for him because Moses felt slow of speech.
Joshua served Moses and led Israel later, but he was not the appointed spokesman to Pharaoh.
Jethro gave Moses wise advice on judging the people, but Aaron was his voice before Pharaoh.

questions.text: How many plagues did God send on Egypt?

options.explanation: There were more than seven. The full count is given across several chapters of Exodus.
Exodus 7 through 12 describes ten plagues, ending with the death of the firstborn.
Twelve is the number of the tribes of Israel, not the plagues. There were ten plagues.
Three is far too few. Egypt was struck with ten plagues in all.

questions.text: What was the final plague on Egypt?

options.explanation: Locusts were one of the earlier plagues, not the last one.
Exodus 12 records the death of every firstborn in Egypt as the final and most severe plague.
The darkness was the ninth plague. The tenth and final one was the death of the firstborn.
Water turning to blood was the very first plague, not the last.

questions.text: What were the Israelites told to put on their doorposts so the plague of death would pass over them?

options.explanation: It was not oil. God told them to use the blood of the Passover lamb.
Exodus 12 instructs them to put the blood of the lamb on the two side posts and the lintel of their houses.
Ashes are not mentioned here. The sign on the doorposts was the blood of the lamb.
No writing was placed on the doors. The mark that brought protection was the lamb's blood.

questions.text: What body of water did God part so Israel could escape Pharaoh's army?

options.explanation: The Jordan was parted later under Joshua. The escape from Egypt was through the Red Sea.
Exodus 14 describes the waters of the Red Sea dividing so Israel walked through on dry ground.
The Sea of Galilee appears in the Gospels, far from the Exodus route.
The Nile turned to blood in the first plague, but the great crossing was at the Red Sea.

questions.text: What did God give the people each morning to eat in the wilderness?

options.explanation: They had left Egypt behind. God provided food in a new and surprising way.
Exodus 16 tells how manna appeared on the ground each morning like a small round thing for the people to gather.
They remembered the fish of Egypt, but in the wilderness God gave manna instead.
The daily provision was manna. Honey was a picture of the promised land, not the wilderness bread.

questions.text: On which mountain did God give Moses the Ten Commandments?

options.explanation: Mount Carmel is where Elijah faced the prophets of Baal much later.
Exodus 19 and 20 place the giving of the commandments at Mount Sinai, where God came down in fire and smoke.
Mount Moriah is where Abraham went to offer Isaac, back in Genesis.
Mount Ararat is where Noah's ark came to rest. The Law was given at Sinai.

questions.text: What was the first of the Ten Commandments?

options.explanation: Keeping the sabbath is one of the commandments, but it is not the first one.

options.text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me
options.explanation: Exodus 20:3 (ASV) reads, "Thou shalt have no other gods before me."
Not stealing is one of the commandments, but it comes later in the list.

options.text: Honor thy father and thy mother
options.explanation: Honoring parents is a commandment too, yet the first one is about having no other gods before God.

scoring.perfectMessage: You parted that quiz like the Red Sea!

gradeBands.message: You know the journey out of Egypt well.

gradeBands.message: Outstanding. You know this story inside and out.
